title: [R3-2] Replace the 127.0.0.2 manager session cookie with a port-bound credential
description:
FILED FROM THE THIRD HUMAN REVIEW OF PR #3 (anchored d01c3316, 2026-08-28: 'Request changes - do not merge', 12 P1 merge blockers + P2 follow-ups). Re-verified at HEAD a09b11fa by a read-only verifier; see the ruling memo in the epic channel. Reviewer's finding: R3-2 manager cookie port. Existing rows checked: task-e868ea339a0d408e8bc9533985b3d92a(DONE) closesIt=false, task-527bab5d07034a52bbf1a1737f0f801c(DONE) closesIt=false, task-164fdb12678744c68ffd80c80d69bc9d(DONE) closesIt=false, task-959df79da24442eeb84d446284ff3357(DONE) closesIt=false, task-ea0106d72cbf48b99236aa6d52b2449b(BLOCKED) closesIt=false, task-c289b8fbcb9840968a9b3994e73b79a4(BLOCKED) closesIt=false. Gap this row closes: No row on the board (search_tasks for cookie/port/127.0.0.2/HttpOnly/port-bound/IPC returned nothing relevant; on-disk grep of every .moe/tasks/*.json confirms) names the manager cookie's lack of a port boundary, an attacker listener on a second 127.0.0.2 port, or replacing the cookie with a port-bound credential or OS IPC channel. Every row that touched project-manager-http*.ts is DONE with a tracking/wiring/pairing-approval DoD, and the two open rows on the surface (task-ea0106d7, task-c289b8fb) would leave routing.ts:176 and contract.ts:192-200 byte-identical. The mechanism is unchanged since d01c3316 and no test in the daemon or tests/security exercises a cross-port cookie replay.

Third human review of PR #3 (anchored at d01c3316, P1 merge blocker R3-2): the project-manager browser session cookie is stealable through another port. The cookie is scoped to host 127.0.0.2 and Path=/manager, but cookies are not port-scoped (apps/daemon/src/projects/project-manager-http-routing.ts:151-180; apps/daemon/src/projects/project-manager-http.ts:112-146). The reviewer REPRODUCED it: the production cookie is sent by the browser to a different 127.0.0.2 port; a same-user worker can bind that port, capture the HttpOnly cookie, obtain the public CSRF token, and replay manager mutations. SameSite/HttpOnly/__Host- cannot establish a port boundary; use a port-bound authorization channel or OS IPC.

RE-MEASURED AT HEAD a09b11fa (both files have zero commits in d01c3316..HEAD and are clean in the worktree, so the reviewer's bytes are HEAD's bytes): project-manager-http.ts:112-114 binds host 127.0.0.2 on the assumption that host partitioning suffices; :82-89 mints ONE randomUUID session secret for the process lifetime; project-manager-main.ts:64 fixes the port at 39122. routing.ts:176 emits `set-cookie: moe_manager_session=<sessionSecret>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/manager` (RFC 6265 has no port attribute). routing.ts:88-104 GET /manager/bootstrap returns csrfToken to any Host-matching caller with no session, so the CSRF token is public. routing.ts:63-82 hostFault/mutationFault check only attacker-suppliable headers (Host, Origin, x-moe-manager-csrf, x-moe-manager-protocol) and then contract.ts:192-200 requestHasSession, which accepts any Cookie header equal to the secret with no binding to port, connection or peer. Reachable with the stolen cookie: GET /manager/projects; POST /manager/projects/create|register; POST /manager/projects/<id>/start|stop|open (routing.ts:258-272). A non-elevated same-user node process on this host bound 127.0.0.2:55236 without error, so the attacker listener needs no privilege. No arm in project-manager-http.test.ts, project-manager-http-refusals.test.ts or tests/security starts a second 127.0.0.2 listener or replays the cookie from a non-browser peer. Contrast: the 127.0.0.1 project daemons already return the credential once in the claim body (pairing-approval-handshake.ts:18-24 PairingClaimed.sessionCredential) and carry it on the origin-bound x-moe-session-credential header; the manager is the only surface on a cookie. docs/agent-stack-runbook.md:30 documents the cookie and must follow the change.
definitionOfDone: DoD-1 red-first cross-port reproduction on the real listener: a focused daemon test starts startProjectManagerHttp on 127.0.0.2:0 and a second plain node:http server on another 127.0.0.2 port in the same (non-elevated) process, runs the legitimate request -> approve -> claim journey, then feeds every manager response header through an RFC 6265 host-only cookie jar keyed on host+path ONLY (port-blind, as a real browser is) and issues GET http://127.0.0.2:<otherPort>/manager/projects; the arm asserts the attacker listener receives no header or body byte containing the manager session credential. At HEAD bytes the arm is red with `moe_manager_session=<secret>` captured; quote that red output in a task comment. Drill: re-add the Set-Cookie line to the claim reply in a %TEMP% copy and confirm this named arm reds again, restore proven by SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup in a separate call.

DoD-2 stolen-credential replay refuses at the credential channel, not at a header fence: an attacker client presents the correct Host `127.0.0.2:<managerPort>`, Origin `http://127.0.0.2:<managerPort>`, the CSRF token read from an unauthenticated GET /manager/bootstrap, the protocol header, and the legitimately minted credential on a Cookie header; every mutation route (/manager/projects/create, /register, /<id>/start|stop|open) and GET /manager/projects refuse with exactly PROJECT_MANAGER_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED at PROJECT_MANAGER_HTTP_LAYER, /manager/bootstrap reports authenticated:false, and the ProjectManagerPort spies (create/register/open/start/stop) have zero calls. Divergence per epic rail 7A: because Host/Origin/CSRF/protocol are all valid, the credential channel is the only mechanism that can refuse. Drill: make requestHasSession (or its replacement) accept the Cookie header again; the AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED arm must red while the HOST/ORIGIN/CSRF arms stay green.

DoD-3 legitimate journey green over a port-bound channel with zero cookies: the Control Room client (apps/control-room/src/v2/projects/project-manager-client.ts) completes bootstrap -> pair request -> claim -> list -> one mutation against a real startProjectManagerHttp listener using the new channel (credential returned once in the claim body and carried on a request header bound to origin http://127.0.0.2:<port>, or an OS IPC handshake); an arm records every response header of the journey and asserts zero `set-cookie` occurrences, and the cookie-parsing branch in project-manager-http-contract.ts:192-200 is deleted rather than left as dead code. Drill: emit one Set-Cookie on any response; the zero-set-cookie arm reds by name.

DoD-4 hostile roster: tests/security gains a boundary-roster entry for the manager port boundary with BEFORE (no credential), AFTER (credential presented via the wrong channel: Cookie header), and RACE (attacker listener bound on a second 127.0.0.2 port before the claim) arms, asserting exact code/layer and a nonzero generated case count over a roster of attacker ports; the existing task-164fdb12 secrecy arms (credential absent from stdout, argv, URL) stay green and one is drilled. Drill: empty the attacker-port roster; the nonzero-count assertion reds.

DoD-5 gates and docs: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` exit 0 with the `$ tsc` script echo quoted; `pnpm exec vitest run` on the manager suites prints nonzero Test Files/Tests lines; `pnpm test:security` runs standalone and unpiped with its exit code and count line recorded; any foreign red is attributed merge-base vs owned-path delta and disclosed verbatim; docs/agent-stack-runbook.md:28-32 no longer describes a manager cookie and names the port-bound channel; no touched production file exceeds 400 lines (routing.ts is 276, contract.ts 255 and client.ts 284 at HEAD: split before growing).
taskRails: No cookie attribute (SameSite, HttpOnly, Secure, __Host-, Path, Domain, Partitioned) may be offered as the fix or as evidence: RFC 6265 has no port scope and the reviewer reproduced the theft against exactly these attributes. Any DoD arm that only inspects Set-Cookie attributes is not evidence.

The attacker fixture's cookie jar MUST key on host+path only and MUST NOT key on port; a port-aware jar is a fixed-point fixture that cannot go red at HEAD and proves nothing (epic rail 7A tell: loosen the guard and the suite stays green).

Prefer the transport the 127.0.0.1 project daemons already use (credential returned once in the claim body, carried on an origin-bound request header) over inventing a new mechanism; fall back to OS IPC only if the header channel cannot satisfy DoD-1. Do not change the 127.0.0.1 listener.

Keep the operator-approval pairing semantics from task-959df79d and task-527bab5d unchanged: one approved request mints one credential exactly once; never reintroduce a bearer in a URL fragment, argv, or stdout (task-164fdb12 secrecy arms must stay green).

Owned paths by explicit pathspec only: apps/daemon/src/projects/project-manager-http.ts, project-manager-http-routing.ts, project-manager-http-contract.ts and their tests, apps/control-room/src/v2/projects/project-manager-client.ts and its test, the tests/security roster entry, docs/agent-stack-runbook.md. Re-measure the bytes at claim (the fleet shares this worktree) and adopt any foreign WIP on these paths only after provenance reconciliation.
TDD: DoD-1 red at HEAD bytes before any production edit, quoted verbatim; drills run in a %TEMP% copy, never in the shared worktree; every drill restore proven by SHA256 in a separate call.
Adopt, never duplicate: re-measure the cited lines at claim time; if a sibling row landed the mechanism first, verify and close rather than re-implement.
